title: 6.22.4 Lab: Lay the trail
description: The whole board from one line of text: rows that snake back and forth, and a token that steps along them to prove the order.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The board is empty and the top says `Square 0 of -1`. `makePath` hands back an empty list, so there are no squares to draw or stand on.

steps.title: One square per letter
steps.instructions: In `makePath`, loop `i` from 0 up to `track.length`. For each one, work out the row `r = floor(i / COLS)` and the column `c = i % COLS`, then push `{ x: c * SIZE + SIZE / 2, y: TOP + r * SIZE + SIZE / 2, kind: track[i] }` onto `squares`. Run: four rows of squares appear.
hints: Make `c` a `let`: the next step changes it.
The y has `TOP` added so the board sits below the words.

steps.title: Snake the odd rows
steps.instructions: Press SPACE to step the token along. At the end of the first row it jumps back to the left edge. Turn every odd row around: `if (r % 2 === 1) c = COLS - 1 - c;`, before the push. Now square 10 sits right below square 9 and the token walks one long winding path.
hints: Count the colours: each letter of `TRACK` is one square, so a J, S, W or F shows where its letter is.

requirements.title: A loop over the track
requirements.description: makePath loops over every letter of the track. Help: 6.22.2 (Reading: A path is a list of squares)

requirements.title: An odd row is turned around
requirements.description: On an odd row the column is counted from the other side, so the path snakes. Help: 6.22.2 (Reading: A path is a list of squares)

requirements.title: Each square keeps x, y and kind
requirements.description: Each square pushed onto the list has an x, a y and its letter as kind. Help: 6.22.2 (Reading: A path is a list of squares)
requirements.hint: squares.push({ x: c * SIZE + SIZE / 2, y: TOP + r * SIZE + SIZE / 2, kind: track[i] });

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Lab: Lay the trail". The task: fill in makePath so it loops over the track text, works out each square's row and column from its index, turns odd rows around so the path snakes, and pushes { x, y, kind } for every square. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: One square per letter
rubric.description: The loop runs over the whole track.

rubric.title: The path snakes
rubric.description: Odd rows run the other way.

rubric.title: x, y and kind
rubric.description: Each square keeps its centre and its letter.
